args.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: ONE isolated low-poly 3D map-landmark concept, square 1:1 PNG, ideally 1536 x 1536. One object only, not a gallery, contact sheet, diagram, photograph or game screenshot. Create a completely NEW whole image.
Reference role: Image 1 is the LOWER UNIFIED SERIES cropped from the supplied map board. Match its very simple faceted forms and MATTE SEPIA color ramp from pale sand/cream through tan to dark brown. It is a STYLE reference only. Do not copy its map-paper background, names, text, cast shadows, other icons, old object errors or multiple-object layout. Follow the revised shape specification below even where the old code icon in the board differs.
Visual language: simple, immediately recognizable in one second, few broad clean polygonal faces and strongly readable silhouette, restrained flat self-shading, like a lightweight game mesh. A narrow sepia-only palette: pale creamy sand highlights, honey/tan midtones, medium umber and deep dark brown recesses. NO photographic surface texture, realistic grain, moss, weathering noise, shiny or metallic material, saturated colors, white/blue snow or green vegetation. Soft diffuse light differentiates object faces without casting a ground shadow. All surfaces matte. No fancy studio realism, no cinematic effects or depth blur.
Camera: consistent orthographic three-quarter view from ABOVE, approximately35 degrees downward and45 degrees around the object. Show the top and two sides. Object upright, with its bottom level, not tilted on its side. Keep the whole silhouette and all tips inside the square with comfortable margins.
Background: completely uniform SOLID very pale warm ivory, no paper/map texture, no horizon, no vignette, no gradient and no floor or surface. NO GROUND BASE, terrain island, pedestal, presentation plinth or slab. NO CAST SHADOW onto the background, NO ambient grounding shadow or drop-shadow halo. Only the object itself and its internal self-shading. Background remains the same light flat color around and below it.
No labels, numbers, letters, writing, logo, watermark, scale bar, interface, frame, people, animals or extra objects. Do not draw the reference board or a comparison sheet. Exactly one finished landmark per image.

COLOSSEUM — LATEST APPROVED CORRECTION OVERRIDES THE OLD BOARD: show ONLY THE SURVIVING HALF of the OUTER PERIMETER WALL, not a complete oval arena. The object is a wide, low, upright approximately180-degree SEMI-ELLIPTICAL WALL ARC with TWO OPEN CUT ENDS. Its outside façade clearly has THREE STACKED ROWS OF ROUND ARCHES and one SOLID UPPERMOST ATTIC level. The three arcade levels and solid fourth level must be clearly separated, not a smooth featureless bow. Simplify to a readable rhythm of large arch openings and clean supports. The curve and both end cross-sections reveal a thick partial outer shell. The missing other half must be completely absent: DO NOT complete the oval using a lower wall, inner seating ring, front rim, platform or arena disc. No sand floor, base slab or ground. Empty ivory background is visible in the open middle and through unobstructed arch openings. Match the board's tan/umber matte low-poly style; avoid tiny realistic stone textures or rubble. Keep the monument WIDE and LOW: roughly80% of square width and around40% of image height, lower edge around y=85%. Its upper wall is lower in this common canvas scale than the Matterhorn or windmill targets. No lettering.
Final check: ONE simple matte SEPIA object, isolated on a perfectly uniform light ivory field, no ground base or ground shadow, no text, no photographic texture. Never output multiple landmarks.

Use a few broad clean angular faces in sepia tan and dark brown. Integrate a small SNOW CAP around the bent top using the LIGHTEST CREAM-SAND SEPIA in the same palette, never white or blue. The light cap follows the upper mountain facets and is not a separate floating hat. The mountain has a natural polygonal foot belonging to the mountain mass itself, but NO additional terrain pad, rocky island, circle, slab, ground plane or shadow below it. ABSOLUTELY NO boat or ship at the edge, no water, trees, rocks arranged around it, buildings, people or extra objects. The mountain is the tallest of this three-icon family: around75-80% of the common square canvas height, with a narrower footprint roughly45-55% of canvas width, bottom near y=85%. Whole peak and all edges visible. Very simple matte faceted sepia game-map model, no photographic geology or snow texture.

KINDERDIJK: ONE SMALL DUTCH OCTAGONAL THATCHED SMOCK WINDMILL, taller than it is wide. The tapering body has a clearly EIGHT-SIDED plan, with broad flat visible facets and a simple thatched warm-tan roof/smock treatment indicated only by clean geometry and slightly different sepia faces, NO photographic straw grain. A compact matte dark-brown rotating CAP sits on top. A SHORT SHAFT protrudes from the CENTER OF THE CAP'S FRONT FACE. Put the single central sail HUB directly on that shaft, physically touching/attached to the CAP, not on the tower's side, not halfway down the body, not floating beside it.
Exactly FOUR SAILS radiate evenly at90-degree intervals from this ONE HUB in a clean X cross. Every sail is connected to the same cap-front axis and all four tips are visible. Simple dark-brown sail frames and a few broad tan panels, no tiny lattice clutter. Do not make a three-bladed turbine, extra mill, detached cross, miscentered blades or sails attached to a lower façade. One modest dark door and at most two very simple window recesses are enough. No balcony deck, platform, terrain island, ground, cast shadow or extra props. Around60-65% of the common square canvas height; smaller and lower than the Matterhorn, taller than the low Colosseum, with a modest narrow body. Whole four-sail silhouette fits comfortably within the square. Same matte low-poly sepia family as the board.
Final check: ONE simple matte SEPIA object, isolated on a perfectly uniform light ivory field, no ground base or ground shadow, no text, no photographic texture. Never output multiple landmarks.
